title: Execution-equality seed (fixture dataset.json shape)
description: T-1b's input: what a database holds BEFORE the fixture's query runs. The engine loads these rows into the table named by the fixture's schema.json `source`, then the compiled query is executed against them and compared with expectedRows.json (XEQ-1..XEQ-4 in spec/semantics.md). Rows are keyed by LOGICAL colId, never by a physical column, so one seed serves every backend; each backend's harness maps colId to its own physical name through the schema's `physical` block. A fixture carries dataset.json and expectedRows.json together or neither. This file is NOT rowStream.json: a seed is what is stored before the query, a row stream is what an adapter yields after it. Value encodings are decided by each field's declared GridSchema type and are specified in XEQ-2; this schema can only say a cell is a scalar, so a runner (and the C# guard test) checks each cell against the field's own type.

rows.description: The seeded rows. At least one: a seed with no rows cannot tell a correct compiler from one that returns nothing.

row.description: One stored row, keyed by logical colId. Every field declared in the fixture's schema.json MUST appear; a null is written as an explicit JSON null, never by omitting the key (XEQ-2), so a reader can tell 'null' from 'forgot'.

additionalProperties.description: One cell. Never an object or an array: v1 seeds are flat.

why.description: Why this row is in the seed: the boundary it sits on, the case variant it tests, the null it carries, the wrong implementation it catches. Optional in the schema so a tool can emit a bare seed, but every authored fixture states it (a row nobody can justify is a row that stops discriminating when the suite changes).
